summary: On node1, added /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/10-complexity.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3. pam_pwquality was already wired into /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth via authselect, so no PAM stack changes were needed. Verified enforcement with real passwd changes as a non-root test user (boundary tests: 11 chars/3 classes rejected, 12 chars/1 class rejected, 12 chars/3 classes accepted, 14 chars/4 classes accepted), confirmed by unchanged vs. changed shadow hashes. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and healthy system state, issued `systemctl reboot` via a detached background command so the ack returned first, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed the boot_id changed, confirmed the policy file and PAM wiring persisted, and re-ran the weak/strong password enforcement test post-reboot with the same pass/fail results. All test users were removed afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected existing PAM/pwquality configuration on node1
Created a test user and set an initial password via chpasswd
Verified an 8-char single-class password is rejected by passwd (hash unchanged)
Verified a 14-char 4-class password is accepted (hash changed)
Verified an 11-char 3-class password is rejected (length boundary)
Verified a 12-char 1-class password is rejected (class boundary)
Verified a 12-char 3-class password is accepted (exact policy boundary)
Captured baseline boot_id and system health on node1
Restarted node1 via backgrounded systemctl reboot so the exec ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed boot_id changed
Confirmed policy file and PAM wiring persisted after reboot
Re-verified weak-password rejection and strong-password acceptance post-reboot with a second test user

evidence.requirement: Password policy configured: minlen=12, minclass=3 on node1
evidence.summary: Inspected existing pwquality.conf and PAM wiring, then wrote minlen=12/minclass=3 to a new drop-in file

evidence.requirement: Enforcement proof: weak passwords rejected, compliant passwords accepted (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Live passwd changes as a non-root user: 8-char and 11-char and 12-char/1-class passwords rejected (shadow hash unchanged), 14-char/4-class and 12-char/3-class passwords accepted (shadow hash changed), proving the exact 12-length/3-class boundary
Removed first test user and its lingering session

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restart on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (cce73776-...), systemctl is-system-running=running, and pwquality config present

evidence.requirement: Node1 restarted one at a time with ack returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot; exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed, proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Polled node1 through connection timeouts/resets during reboot until reachable again; boot_id changed from cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 to 29682ff7-cc94-48be-9fae-1edbc8257a69

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: system healthy and policy config/PAM wiring intact
evidence.summary: systemctl is-system-running=running; pwquality.conf.d file and pam_pwquality entries in system-auth/password-auth confirmed present after reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof the policy is actively enforced, not just present on disk
evidence.summary: Created a second test user post-reboot; a weak 7-char password was rejected (hash unchanged) and a compliant 12-char/3-class password was accepted (hash changed) via live passwd change, then test user removed
